glossary.lǫst: lǫstr (m.) — fault, vice, blame; here acc. sg. (án við lǫst 'without vice')
glossary.maga: magi (m.) — belly, stomach; here gen. sg. (mál maga 'the measure of the belly')
glossary.magran: magr — lean, thin; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.man: man (n.) — a bondwoman, a girl, a young woman; nom. or acc. sg. (it horska man is the subject at st. 102; it manunga man is the subject of mun … firraz at st. 162,3, nom. sg. — the nom. and acc. of a neuter noun are alike, so the form alone does not show it, and mik is the accusative object of firraz).
glossary.mann: maðr (m.) — man; here acc. sg. (mildan mann 'a generous man')
glossary.manna: maðr (m.) — man; here gen. pl. (manna hverr 'each of men')
glossary.manngi: manngi — no one, no man (nom. sg.); nýtr manngi nás; leiðiz manngi gott, ef getr (st. 130,10). At 130,10 the Codex Regius first wrote margr 'many a man' and its own scribe corrected it to mangi; Neckel prints manngi.
glossary.manni: maðr (m.) — man; here dat. sg., 'to/for a man'
glossary.mannz: maðr (m.) — man; here gen. sg. (mannz gaman 'man's delight'; snotrs mannz)
glossary.mannzkis: manngi — no one; in a negative clause 'anyone'; here gen. sg. (né mannzkis gaman 'nor any man's pleasure')
glossary.mans: man (n.) — girl, young woman; here gen. sg.
glossary.manunga: manungr — youthful, in the bloom of youth; here weak acc. sg. neut., agreeing with man
glossary.mar: marr (m.) — steed, horse; here acc. sg. (magran mar kaupa 'buy a lean horse'). A different word from marr (m.) 'sea', also acc. mar (aldinn mar 'the ancient sea').
glossary.marga: margr — many; here acc. pl. (marga staði 'many places')
glossary.margan: margr — many a; here acc. sg. masc. (um margan … guma 'over many a man')
glossary.margfróðr: margfróðr — knowing much, widely learned (margr + fróðr); nom. sg. masc.
glossary.margir: margr — many; here nom. pl. masc. (Gumnar margir 'many men')
glossary.margr: margr — many a one, many (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.mart: margr — much, many things; here neut. (mart gengr verr; mæli til mart 'speaks too much')
glossary.mat: matr (m.) — food; here acc. sg., the object of villat (mat þú villat 'food you want not', st. 114,4); also after a preposition (at málungi mat 'food at mealtime').
glossary.matar: matr (m.) — food; here gen. sg. (matar þǫrf 'need of food')
glossary.mega: mega — to be able, to have the power; here infinitive (gørva mega 'to be able to make')
glossary.megi: mega — may, can; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'may' (er vinnaz megi 'which may last')
glossary.megin: megin (n.) — might, main strength; here acc. sg. (iarðar megin 'the earth's strength')
glossary.mego: mega — to be able, may; here 3rd pl. pres., 'can' (mego … leyna 'can hide')
glossary.mein: mein (n.) — harm, hurt, injury; here nom. pl., the subject of eta
glossary.meira: meiri — more; here neut. comparative (en meira 'and more')
glossary.meiði: meiðr (m.) — a tree, a pole, a beam; here dat. sg. (vindga meiði á 'on a windy tree'; á þeim meiði 'on that tree')
glossary.mettr: metta — to feed, sate; here past participle masc., 'fed, sated' (Þveginn ok mettr)
glossary.mey: mær (f.) — maiden, girl; acc. sg. (Billings mey; mey né mannz kono, st. 163,3). At 163,3 the case is a wrinkle worth naming: kenna 'to teach' normally takes the dative of the person taught, and þeiri einni in line 7 of the same stanza is dative, but mey is accusative and kono could be either, kona having one form for both. Neckel prints the manuscript's words and the mismatch stands.
glossary.meyiar: mær (f.) — maiden, girl; here gen. sg. (meyiar orðom 'a maiden's words'); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.mikil: mikill — great, much; here nom. sg. fem., agreeing with þǫrf (þǫrf mikil 'great need')
glossary.mikils: mikill — great, much; here gen. as adv., 'much' (Mikils til snemma 'much too early')
glossary.mikit: mikill — great, much; here neut., 'much' (manvit mikit 'much good sense')
glossary.mildan: mildr — generous, liberal; here acc. sg. masc. (mildan mann)
glossary.mildir: mildr — generous, liberal; here nom. pl. masc. (Mildir menn 'generous men')
glossary.min: minn — my; here nom. sg. fem. (min systir 'my sister'). Neckel prints it without the acute at 163,9, beside míno at 154,3.
glossary.minn: minn — my; here acc. sg. masc. (í minn frama 'to my own advantage')
glossary.minna: minn — my; here gen. pl. (minna andskota 'of my adversaries')
glossary.minnigr: minnigr — of good memory, mindful (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.misseri: misseri (n.) — a half-year, season; here acc. sg. (mál ok misseri)
glossary.miǫk: miǫk — much, very, greatly (adv.); Neckel's spelling with ǫ (later Icelandic mjök)
glossary.miǫt: miǫt (n.) — measure, due amount; here acc. sg. (kann miǫt 'knows the measure')
glossary.miǫð: miǫðr (m.) — mead; here acc. sg. (drekki miǫð 'drink mead')
glossary.morgin: morginn (m.) — morning; here acc. sg. (um morgin søfr 'sleeps through the morning')
glossary.morni: morginn (m.) — morning; here dat. sg. (at morni kømr 'comes in the morning')
glossary.mun: munu — shall, will; here 3rd sg. pres. (þat mun æ vera 'that will ever be')
glossary.munar: munr (m.) — desire, longing, delight; here gen. sg.
glossary.munat: munu — shall, will; here 3rd sg. pres. with the suffixed negative -at, 'he will not'
glossary.mundo: munu — shall, will; here 2nd sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun fused on (munt þú → mundo), 'you will'.
glossary.munn: munnr (m.) — mouth; here acc. sg. (Rata munn 'Rati's mouth')
glossary.muno: munu — shall, will (auxiliary); 3rd pl. pres., 'they will (be)' (þér muno góð, ef þú getr, the Loddfáfnir refrain); also the infinitive (muno ey lifa 'will live forever').
glossary.munoð: munoð (f.) — love, desire, pleasure; here acc. sg. (flióðs munoð 'a woman's love')
glossary.munr: munr (m.) — mind, desire, longing, delight (nom. sg.)
glossary.munt: munu — shall, will; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you will' (Rúnar munt þú finna)
glossary.munðu: munu — shall, will; here 2nd sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun þú (munt þú → munðu), 'you will'. Neckel prints the ð; the same letters would also spell the imperative of muna 'to remember', but vanr vera in the next line requires the auxiliary.
glossary.mynda: munu — shall, will; here 1st sg. pret. subjunctive, 'I would'
glossary.myndi: munu — shall, will; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'would' (myndi mér heim of boðit 'I would be invited home')
glossary.myrkri: myrkr (n.) — darkness, the dark; here dat. sg.
glossary.má: mega — to be able, to have the power, may; here 1st sg. pres., 'I may, I can' (at ek ganga má 'that I may walk', st. 149,5; þat má ek bœta brátt 'that I can soon mend', st. 153,4)
glossary.mál: mál (n.) — measure; mealtime; speech, a saying; the right time. Acc. sg. (mál maga 'measure of the belly'; í mál hvert 'at every mealtime'; manna mál 'the speech of men'); nom. sg. with an infinitive (Mál er at þylia 'it is time to chant'). At st. 164,1, Nú ero Háva mál kveðin, it is NOM. PL. NEUT., the subject of ero, with kveðin and allþǫrf/óþǫrf all agreeing with it — the plural that gives the poem its title, Hávamál 'the sayings of Hávi'.
glossary.máli: mál (n.) — speech; here dat. sg. (at máli kuðr 'known by his speech')
glossary.máls: mál (n.) — speech, a saying; here gen. sg. governed by gá (þióðans máls 'a lord's speech')
glossary.málugr: málugr — talkative, ready of speech (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.málungi: málungi — from meal to meal, at mealtime; (at málungi mat 'food for the meal')
glossary.mána: máni (m.) — the moon; here acc. sg.
glossary.mánaði: mánaðr (m.) — month; here dat. sg. (á mánaði 'in a month')
glossary.mátki: máttugr (mátkr) — mighty, powerful; here weak nom. sg. masc. (sá inn mátki munr)
glossary.mæki: mækir (m.) — sword, blade; here acc./dat. sg.
glossary.mæla: mæla — to speak (infinitive); fagrt mæla 'speak fair'
glossary.mæli: mæla — to speak; here 1st sg. pres., 'I speak' (bert ek nú mæli); also 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him speak'
glossary.mælir: mæla — to speak; here 3rd sg. pres. (Œrna mælir 'speaks in plenty')
glossary.mælom: mæla — to speak; here 1st pl. pres., 'we speak'
glossary.mælta: mæla — to speak; here 1st sg. pret., 'I spoke'
glossary.mætti: mega — to be able, may; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'could' (ef sér geta mætti 'if he could get')
glossary.mér: ek — I; here dat. sg., 'to/for me' (fekk mér 'got for myself')
glossary.mína: minn — my; here acc. pl. masc. (mína heiptmǫgo 'my foes')
glossary.mínar: minn — my; here nom./acc. pl. fem. (Váðir mínar 'my clothes')
glossary.míno: minn — my; here dat. sg. neut., agreeing with fari
glossary.míns: minn — my; here gen. sg. (míns munar 'my desire')
glossary.mœti: mœta — to meet; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'should meet'
glossary.mǫgr: mǫgr (m.) — son, boy, young man; here nom. sg. (mannzkis mǫgr 'any man's son')
glossary.mǫrg: margr — many, many a; nom. pl. neut. (mǫrg ero dags augo); also nom. sg. fem. (mǫrg er góð mær 'many a good maiden is')
glossary.mǫrgom: margr — many; here dat. pl. (með mǫrgom 'among many')
glossary.nam: nema — to take, to take in, to learn; here pret. sg., 1st and 3rd alike. Four constructions in this part: nema upp 'to take up' (nam ek upp rúnar, st. 139,4); absolutely, of the runes just named (œpandi nam 'screaming I took them', 139,6); nema af e-m 'to learn from someone' (nam ek af inom frægia syni, 140,2); with a following infinitive, 'to begin, to take to' (nam ek frævaz, 141,1); and, in the closing stanza, 3rd sg. of taking in what has been chanted (Nióti, sá er nam!, 164,7).
glossary.nauðr: nauðr (f.) — need, distress, constraint; here nom. sg. (ef mik nauðr um stendr 'if need presses upon me')
glossary.neiss: neiss — put to shame, disgraced (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.nem: nema — to take; to learn; here imperative sg. (nem líknargaldr 'learn a healing-charm')
glossary.nema: nema — unless, except (conj.); nema þeiri einni 'except to her alone' (st. 163,7). ALSO nema — to take, to take in, to learn; infinitive at st. 153,3, ǫllom … nytsamlikt at nema 'useful for all to take up' — the same verb as the refrain's ef þú nemr and as sá er nam (st. 164,7). Two different words with the same form.
glossary.nemir: nema — to take, to take in, to learn; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive in the Loddfáfnir refrain (at/en þú ráð nemir 'and may you take the counsel'); Neckel prints at þú up to st. 115 and en þú from st. 116 on.
glossary.nemr: nema — to take, to learn; here 2nd sg. pres. indicative (ef þú nemr 'if you take them').
glossary.nesti: nesti (n.) — provisions, travelling-food; here dat. sg. (nesti trúir 'trusts his stores')
glossary.nið: niðr (m.) — kinsman, descendant; here acc./dat. sg. (at nið 'for kinsman')
glossary.niðr: niðr — (1) adverb: down, downwards (nýsta ek niðr 'I peered down', st. 139,3). (2) niðr (m.) — kinsman, descendant; nom. sg. (nema reisi niðr 'unless a kinsman raise'). The inherited entry had only the noun, and the Rúnatal needs the adverb.
glossary.niósn: niósn (f.) — spying, look-out, watch; here dat. sg. (á niósn 'on the watch')
glossary.nióta: nióta (+ gen.) — to have the use of, to profit by, to enjoy the benefit of (infinitive); in the Loddfáfnir refrain (nióta mundo 'you will have use of them') its object is never spoken — the counsels themselves, plural on the evidence of the neuter plural góð in the next line.
glossary.nióti: nióta (+ gen.) — to have the use of, to profit by, to enjoy; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'may he have the use of it'; the genitive it governs is not supplied
glossary.notit: nióta (+ gen.) — to make use of, enjoy, have the benefit of; here past part. (hefi ek vel notit 'I have made good use of')
glossary.nytak: nióta (+ gen.) — to make use of, to have the benefit of; here 1st sg. PRETERITE subjunctive with the enclitic -k 'I' (ne nytak 'had I not had') — the sentence is a past counterfactual
glossary.nytsamlikt: nytsamlikr — useful, profitable, worth having; here nom. sg. neut. (ǫllom … nytsamlikt at nema)
glossary.nái: ná — to reach, get, be able; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (nái … þruma 'gets to sit quiet')
glossary.náir: ná — to reach, attain, be able; here 2nd sg. pres. after ef (ef þú segia ne náir 'if you cannot manage to tell'); indicative and subjunctive are identical in this verb; also 3rd sg. pres. (ef maðr hafa náir).
glossary.nás: nár (m.) — corpse, dead body; here gen. sg. (nýtr manngi nás 'no one has use of a corpse')
glossary.næfra: næfr (f.) — birch-bark; here gen. pl. (þakinna næfra 'of roofing-bark')
glossary.nær: nær — when; near (adv./conj.); also 'towards' with the dative in expressions of time (nær apni 'towards evening', nær morni 'towards morning')
glossary.næst: næst — next, nearest, the next time (adv.)
glossary.nætr: nótt (f.) — night; here acc. pl. (allar nætr 'all nights')
glossary.níunda: níundi — ninth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.nótt: nótt (f.) — night; here the adverbial acc. of time, 'by night' (nótt þú rísat 'do not get up at night'); also acc. sg. as object (Nótt verðr feginn 'glad of night').
glossary.nýfeldom: nýfeldr — newly felled, freshly killed (nýr 'new' + feldr, past part. of fella); here dat. sg.
glossary.nýsiz: nýsa — to peer, investigate; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'feels his way, scouts' (nýsiz fyrir)
glossary.nýsta: nýsa — to peer, to pry, to look searchingly; here 1st sg. pret., 'I peered'
glossary.nýt: nýtr — useful, serviceable, good to have; here nom. pl. neut., standing with góð and þǫrf and agreeing with the same unspoken plural (nýt, ef þú nemr)
glossary.nýta: nýtr — able, doughty, serviceable; here weak nom. sg. fem. (in nýta vígdrótt)
glossary.nýtr: nióta (+ gen.) — to use, enjoy; here 3rd sg. pres. (nýtr manngi nás 'no one enjoys a corpse')
glossary.of: of — about, concerning (prep.; of rúnar dœma 'to discourse of runes'); also an old expletive particle before verbs (of heimtir), and 'over, above'.
glossary.ofblótit: blóta — to sacrifice; here past part. neut. with the prefix of- 'over-, too much', used impersonally with no subject (en sé ofblótit 'than that there be over-offering')
glossary.ofdrykkia: ofdrykkia (f.) — over-drinking, excess in drink; here nom. sg. (ofdrykkia ǫls 'over-drinking of ale')
glossary.ofrǫlvi: ofrǫlvi — dead-drunk, over-drunk (of- intensive + ǫlvi 'drunk'); here nom. sg. masc.
glossary.ofsóit: sóa — to sacrifice, to slay, to make away with; here past part. neut. with of- 'over-', used impersonally (en sé ofsóit 'than that there be over-slaying')
glossary.ofvaran: ofvarr — over-wary, too cautious (of- 'too much' + varr); here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.orka: orka (+ gen.) — to work, be able, get (something) out of; here infinitive (skriðar orka 'to get speed')
glossary.ormi: ormr (m.) — serpent, snake, worm; here dat. sg.
glossary.orrosto: orrosta (f.) — battle, fight; dat. sg. after í (í orrosto — the í was added above the line by the Codex Regius scribe) and gen. sg. after til (til orrosto leiða 'to lead to battle', st. 156,2).
glossary.orz: orð (n.) — word, speech; here gen. sg. (orz ok endrþǫgo 'of speech and silence-in-return')
glossary.orztírr: orztírr (m.) — fame, glory, good repute (orð 'word' + tírr 'glory'); here nom. sg.
glossary.orð: orð (n.) — word, speech. Nom. sg. (orð … orz leitaði 'a word sought out a word', st. 141,4). Also nom./acc. pl. (orð illrar kono, the accusative subject of bíta at st. 118; skilin orð koma, st. 134,9). The inherited entry gave only the plural.
glossary.orða: orð (n.) — word; here gen. pl. (orða þeira 'of those words')
glossary.orði: orð (n.) — word; here dat. sg. of source (af orði 'from a word')
glossary.ramt: rammr — strong, mighty; here nom. sg. neut. (ramt er þat tré)
glossary.randir: rǫnd (f.) — the rim of a shield, and so the shield itself; here acc. pl. after und (und randir 'in under the shields')
glossary.rangt: rangr — crooked, awry, wrong; here nom. sg. neut.
glossary.rata: Rati (m.) — Rati, the auger that bored the way into the mountain; here gen. sg.
glossary.ratar: rata — to travel, wander, roam; here 3rd sg. pres., 'travels' (víða ratar 'travels widely')
glossary.reginkunnom: reginkunnr — sprung from the gods, of divine descent (regin 'the powers' + -kunnr 'descended'); here dat. pl.
glossary.reis: rísa — to rise; here 3rd sg. pret., 'he rose' (þar hann upp um reis)
glossary.reisi: reisa — to raise, set up; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'raise' (nema reisi niðr 'unless a kinsman raise')
glossary.reist: rísta — to cut, to carve (runes); here 1st and 3rd sg. pret., 'carved'
glossary.rekkar: rekkr (m.) — warrior, man; here nom. pl. (rekkar þóttoz 'they seemed warriors')
glossary.rekr: reka — to drive; here 3rd sg. pres. (hiǫrð rekr 'drives a herd')
glossary.renn: renna — to run; of a plant, to spring, to have its source; here 3rd sg. pres. (hvers hann af rótom renn)
glossary.reynda: reyna — to try, test, learn by experience; here 1st sg. pret.
glossary.reyndr: reyna — to try, test; here past part. masc. sg., 'tried, tested'
glossary.reynt: reyna — to try, prove; here past part. neut. sg., 'proved'
glossary.reyri: reyrr (m.) — reed, reed-bed; here dat. sg.
glossary.ript: ript (f.) — a piece of cloth, garment; here acc. sg. (ript hǫfðo 'had cloth')
glossary.ro: vera — to be; here 3rd pl. pres., 'are' (an old form of ero); Tveir ro; skammar ro
glossary.rár: rá (f.) — a sail-yard; here nom. pl. (skips rár 'a ship's yards')
glossary.rás: rás — the first element of the compound Neckel prints open at st. 151,3, rás viðar; formally it is rás (f.) 'a running, a course', but rásviðr 'running-wood' has never been securely construed by any editor. Rendered 'running-tree' in the literal layer as a placeholder, not a construal — see the note to st. 151.
glossary.ráð: ráð (n.) — counsel, advice, plan; nom./acc. pl. (ill ráð 'bad counsel') and acc. in the Loddfáfnir refrain, in the phrase ráð nema 'to take counsel' (en þú ráð nemir). Read as plural in the refrain: the fourth line's neuter plural góð agrees with it.
glossary.ráða: ráða — to counsel; of runes, to interpret, to read; here infinitive (hvé ráða skal 'how one shall read')
glossary.ráðna: ráða — to read, to interpret; here past part. acc. pl. masc. (ráðna stafi 'staves that are read')
glossary.ráðom: ráð (n.) — counsel, plan; here dat. pl. (um ráðom þǫgðo 'were silent about counsels')
glossary.ráðomk: ráða (+ dat. of the person) — to counsel, to advise; here 1st sg. pres. with the -mk middle ending, 'I counsel you' (ráðomk þér). The word that opens every stanza of the Loddfáfnir counsels.
glossary.ráðs: ráð (n.) — counsel, advice, plan; here gen. sg. governed by fregna
glossary.ráðsnotra: ráðsnotr — prudent, wise in counsel; here gen./acc. (ráðsnotra hverr 'every prudent man')
glossary.ráðspaka: ráðspakr — wise in counsel; here weak acc. sg. neut., agreeing with flióð
glossary.ræðr: ráða — to rule, govern, decide (+ dat.); with a following infinitive, to undertake or manage to do a thing; here 3rd sg. pres. (hverr er segia ræðr 'whoever undertakes to tell').
glossary.ríki: ríki (n.) — power, authority, realm; acc. sg. (Ríki sitt 'his power') and dat. sg. after með (með ríki fara 'to fare with power', st. 156,5).
glossary.rísa: rísa — to rise (infinitive); ár skal rísa 'should rise early'
glossary.rísat: rísa — to rise, get up; here the imperative sg. with the suffixed negative -at (rís + -at), 'rise not'; the 2nd sg. pres. indicative would be ríss.
glossary.ríst: rísta — to carve, to cut, to cut runes; here 1st sg. pres., 'I carve'
glossary.rísta: rísta — to cut, to carve, to incise (infinitive)
glossary.ríða: ríða — to ride; of a door or a beam, to swing, to turn on its hinge (infinitive)
glossary.ríði: ríða — to ride; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him ride' (ríði maðr þingi at)
glossary.ríðr: ríða — to ride; here 3rd sg. pres., 'rides' (Haltr ríðr hrossi)
glossary.róg: róg (n.) — strife, slander; here nom./acc. sg. (aldar róg 'the strife of men')
glossary.rótlausom: rótlauss — rootless (rót 'root' + -lauss '-less'); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.rótom: rót (f.) — a root; here dat. pl. (hvers hann af rótom renn 'from what roots it runs', st. 138,9; á rótom rás viðar, st. 151,3)
glossary.rúms: rúm (n.) — room, space; here gen. sg. governed by fá
glossary.rúnar: rún (f.) — (1) a rune, a carved character, and the lore that goes with it: acc. pl. at st. 111,7 (of rúnar dœma), 139,4 (nam ek upp rúnar) and 142,1 (Rúnar munt þú finna), and the antecedent of the sumar 'some of them' at 143,5. (2) The older sense 'a secret, a thing confided, a whispered counsel', at work in the compounds eyrarúna (st. 115) and gamanrúnar (st. 120), and in the nom. pl. of 137,14 (en við bǫlvi rúnar).
glossary.rúnom: rún (f.) — rune, secret, mystery; here dat. pl. (at rúnom spyria 'to ask after the runes')
glossary.rýtanda: rýta — to grunt, squeal; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'grunting'
glossary.rǫgna: regin (n. pl.) — the ruling powers, the gods; here gen. pl. (hroptr rǫgna 'Hroptr of the gods'). The same word as in ginnregin and in ragna rǫk.
glossary.rǫk: rǫk (n. pl.) — fate, doom; also the whole course, ground and origin of a thing; here acc. pl. after fyr (fyr þióða rǫk), which is therefore either 'before the doom of peoples' or 'before the beginnings of peoples'. The word of ragna rǫk.
glossary.sal: salr (m.) — hall; acc. sg. (taugreptan sal, st. 36). At st. 152,3 sal um sessmǫgom is the accusative subject of the infinitive loga after sé, 'the hall blazing over the bench-companions'.
glossary.saldrótt: saldrótt (f.) — the hall-troop, the household (salr 'hall' + drótt 'retinue'); nom. sg.
glossary.sama: samr — same; here neut. (it sama 'the same')
glossary.sanda: sandr (m.) — sand; here gen. pl. (lítilla sanda 'of small sands')
glossary.sanna: sannr — true; here strong acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sǫk (um sanna sǫk 'over a true charge'); the weak accusative would be sǫnnu.
glossary.sat: sitia — to sit; here 1st sg. pret., 'I sat'
glossary.saurgan: saurugr — dirty, soiled, grimy; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.sefa: sefi (m.) — mind, feeling, affection; acc. sg. after um (einn er hann sér um sefa); gen. sg. (síns ins svára sefa 'for her heavy spirit'); dat. sg. as the object of snúa, which governs the dative (sný ek hennar ǫllom sefa, st. 161,6).
glossary.sefi: sefi (m.) — mind, heart, feeling (nom. sg.); sorgalausastr sefi
glossary.segia: segia — to say, to tell (infinitive); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.segir: segia — to say; here 3rd sg. pres., 'says' (er maðr ǫðrom segir)
glossary.seint: seinn — slow, late; here neut. sg. used adverbially, 'slowly, late' (mun seint firraz 'will be slow to shun')
glossary.seldo: selia — to hand over, to give, to give in exchange; here 3rd pl. pret. with an indefinite subject, 'they gave'. The line will not construe as printed (see the note to st. 139); Bugge reads sœldo 'refreshed', Eiríkr Magnússon sældo 'gladdened', Sijmons sǫddo 'sated'.
glossary.senda: senda — to send; here infinitive, in the sacrificial list of st. 144, evidently of dispatching an offering — the sense is not certain
glossary.senn: senn — at once, all at once
glossary.senna: senna — to bandy words, to wrangle, to flyte (infinitive; here governed by skalattu, with þrimr orðom as the dative of means, st. 125,5–6); the noun senna is the name of the formal exchange of insults, as in the title Lokasenna.
glossary.sessmǫgom: sessmǫgr (m.) — a bench-companion, one who shares the seat (sess 'seat, bench' + mǫgr 'son, young man'); here dat. pl.
glossary.sextánda: sextándi — sixteenth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.siaunda: siaundi — seventh; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.siautiánda: siautiándi — seventeenth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.sifiom: sifiar (f. pl.) — kinship, the bonds of kin and of marriage; here dat. pl. governed by blanda
glossary.sigr: sigr (m.) — victory; here acc. sg. (né sofandi maðr sigr 'nor a sleeping man victory')
glossary.sik: sik — oneself (acc. reflexive); um sik vera 'to be (prudent) about himself'
glossary.sinn: sinn — his own (reflexive possessive); here acc. sg. (sinn bana 'his own death')
glossary.sinna: sinn — his, her, their own (the reflexive possessive); here gen. pl., agreeing with hama and huga (sinna heim hama 'of their own home-shapes')
glossary.sinni: sinn — his own; here dat. sg. fem. (at hyggiandi sinni 'of his understanding')
glossary.sitia: sitia — to sit; infinitive, and 3rd pl. pres. (þeir er sitia inni fyrir 'those who sit indoors'). Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.sitr: sitia — to sit; here 3rd sg. pres., 'sits'
glossary.sitt: sinn — his own; here nom./acc. sg. neut. (sitt geð 'his own mind')
glossary.siá: siá — this, this one (demonstrative pron., nom. sg. masc.); Neckel's spelling of sjá
glossary.siálfom: siálfr — self; dat. sg. masc. (á siálfom sýnst 'most seen on oneself'; siálfom mér 'to my own self', st. 138,6, the dative governed by gefinn; nema þú siálfom þér sér, st. 126,7).
glossary.siálfr: siálfr — self, himself, myself; nom. sg. masc., agreeing with the subject (siálfr um á 'himself has'; siálfr siálfom mér, st. 138,6, where it agrees with the ek that hung; ek reist siálfr sumar 'I myself carved some', st. 143,5). At 138,6 R adds the word above the line.
glossary.siálfráða: siálfráða (adj., indeclinable) — one's own master, doing as he pleases (siálfr 'self' + ráða 'rule'); here in a dative slot
glossary.sió: siór (sær) (m.) — sea; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.siónom: sión (f.) — sight, the eye; here dat. pl. (siónom of sék 'I see it with my eyes')
glossary.siúkom: siúkr — sick, ill; here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.skal: skulu — shall, must; here pres. sg., 1st and 3rd alike. Personal, 1st sg., in the charm conditions: ef ek skal til orrosto leiða (st. 156,2), ef ek skal þegn ungan verpa vatni á (158,2), ef ek skal fyrða liði telia tíva fyrir (159,2). Impersonal, with an infinitive and no subject, 'one shall' — which is how all eight questions of st. 144 are built (veitstu, hvé rísta skal? 'do you know how one shall carve?'). Neither use was in the inherited entry.
glossary.skala: skulu — 'shall not' (skal + suffixed negative -a); skala maðr 'a man should not'
glossary.skalattu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. with the suffixed negative -at and the enclitic pronoun þú (skalt + -at + þú), 'you shall not'. At 113,6 the Codex Regius first wrote skaltu and corrected it to skalatu, and a cancelled (subpuncted) firra þik stands after it; the same correction is recorded at 125,6.
glossary.skaldu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun þú (skalt þú → skaldu), 'you shall'
glossary.skalt: skulu — shall, must; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you shall'
glossary.skaltu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. + þú, 'you shall' (skaltu = skalt + þú)
glossary.skammar: skammr — short; here nom. pl. fem. (skammar ro skips rár 'short are a ship's yards')
glossary.skammiz: skammask — to be ashamed (middle); here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him be ashamed' (skammiz engi)
glossary.skapaðr: skapa — to shape, to make; here past part. nom. sg. masc. (skór er skapaðr illa 'a shoe is badly made')
glossary.skapi: skap (n.) — temper, disposition; here dat. sg. (illa skapi 'of ill temper')
glossary.skapt: skapt (n.) — a shaft, the wooden handle of a spear or axe; here nom. sg.
glossary.skeptismiðr: skeptismiðr (m.) — a shaft-maker, a wright of spear-shafts (skapt + smiðr); here nom. sg.
glossary.skil: skil (n. pl.) — discernment, the telling of one thing from another; kunna skil e-s 'to know all about, to be able to tell apart'; here acc.
glossary.skilin: skilia — to part, to distinguish, to discern; here past part. nom. pl. neut., 'sifted, clear-cut' (skilin orð)
glossary.skip: skip (n.) — ship; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.skips: skip (n.) — ship; here gen. sg. (skips rár 'a ship's yards')
glossary.skipta: skipta (+ dat.) — to exchange, share; here infinitive (giǫfom skipta 'exchange gifts')
glossary.skiǫld: skiǫldr (m.) — shield; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.skollir: skolla — to dangle, to hang loose, to sway; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.skolo: skulu — shall, must; here 3rd pl. pres. (þær heim skolo 'they must go home')
glossary.skotinn: skióta — to shoot; here past part. acc. sg. masc., agreeing with flein (af fári skotinn flein 'a shaft shot in malice')
glossary.skoðar: skoða — to look at, examine; here 3rd sg. pres., 'looks about'
glossary.skoðaz: skoða — to look over; here with -z middle, 'be scanned' (um skoðaz skyli 'should be scanned')
glossary.skriðar: skriðr (m.) — gliding, headway, a ship's speed; here gen. sg. governed by orka
glossary.skrám: skrá (f.) — a dried skin, a piece of parchment; here dat. pl.
glossary.skríða: skríða — to creep, glide, travel over ice (infinitive)
glossary.skygnaz: skygnaz — to look about, peer around (a -z/-sk middle verb); here pres. subjunctive
glossary.skyli: skulu — shall, ought; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'should' (the gnomic 'one should')
glossary.skíða: skíð (n.) — a billet, split log; here gen. pl. (Þurra skíða 'of dry logs')
glossary.skór: skór (m.) — a shoe; here nom. sg.
glossary.skósmiðr: skósmiðr (m.) — a shoemaker; here nom. sg.
glossary.skúa: skór (m.) — shoe; here gen. pl. (skúa ok bróka 'of shoes and breeches')
glossary.skǫpoð: skapa — to shape, create; here past part. nom. pl. neut., 'shaped'
glossary.skǫrpom: skarpr — shrivelled, dried up, hard; here dat. sg. masc. (ór skǫrpom belg)
glossary.sloknar: slokna — to be quenched, go out; here 3rd sg. pres. (þá sloknar 'then it goes out')
glossary.slíkan: slíkr — such; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.slíkt: slíkr — such; here neut., 'such (is)' (slíkt er 'such is')
glossary.snapir: snapa — to snap (the beak), sniff about; here 3rd sg. pres. (Snapir ok gnapir)
glossary.snotrom: snotr — wise, sensible; dat. sg. or pl. (hveim snotrom manni 'for any wise man'; með snotrom 'among the wise')
glossary.snotrs: snotr — wise; here gen. sg. (snotrs mannz 'of a wise man')
glossary.snópir: snópa — to mope, hang about hungry; here 3rd sg. pres., 'mopes'
glossary.sný: snúa (+ dat.) — to turn, to twist, to turn round; here 1st sg. pres., 'I turn' (sný ek hennar ǫllom sefa)
glossary.sofandi: sofa — to sleep; here pres. participle, 'sleeping' (sofandi maðr)
glossary.sofin: sofa — to sleep; here past part. fem. sg., 'asleep' (saldrótt um sofin)
glossary.sono: sonr (m.) — son; here acc. pl. (hǫlða sono 'the sons of men')
glossary.sonom: sonr (m.) — son; here dat. pl. (alda sonom 'for the sons of men')
glossary.sorgafullr: sorgafullr — full of sorrows (sorg + fullr); here nom. sg. masc.
glossary.sorgalausastr: sorgalauss — free of sorrow; here superlative, 'most sorrow-free' (sorgalausastr sefi)
glossary.sorgom: sorg (f.) — sorrow, grief; here dat. pl.
glossary.sparir: spara — to spare, save up; here 3rd sg. pres. (sparir leiðom 'saves for the hated')
glossary.spialla: spialla — to talk, converse (infinitive); við man spialla 'talk with a girl'
glossary.sprettr: spretta — to spring, to start, to burst off; here 3rd sg. pres. (sprettr mér af fótom fiǫturr)
glossary.spurðo: spyria (+ at) — to ask, ask after; here 3rd pl. pret.
glossary.spyrr: spyria (+ at) — to ask, ask after, enquire; here 2nd sg. pres.
glossary.stafi: stafr (m.) — (1) a letter, a rune-stave — the carved character itself (ráðna stafi, miǫk stóra stafi, miǫk stinna stafi, st. 142,2–4); (2) a staff; (3) by extension a word, a saying (staðlauso stafi 'groundless words'). Acc. pl. throughout. The inherited entry glossed it 'staff; letter, word'; the Rúnatal needs the carved character itself foregrounded.
glossary.standa: standa — to stand; here 3rd pl. pres., 'stand' (bautasteinar standa)
glossary.stað: staðr (m.) — place; here dat. sg. (í ókunnom stað 'in an unknown place')
glossary.staðar: staðr (m.) — place; here gen. sg. governed by leita; leita sér staðar 'to seek oneself a place', the ordinary euphemism for going outside to relieve oneself
glossary.staði: staðr (m.) — place; here acc. pl. (marga staði 'many places')
glossary.staðlauso: staðlauss — without foundation, groundless; here acc. pl. (staðlauso stafi 'groundless words')
glossary.stelr: stela (+ dat.) — to steal; here 3rd sg. pres., 'steals' (stelr geði 'steals the mind')
glossary.stendr: standa — to stand; here 3rd sg. pres. (sú er stendr 'which stands')
glossary.stinna: stinnr — stiff, strong, unyielding; here acc. pl. masc. (miǫk stinna stafi)
glossary.stint: stinnr — stiff, strong; here neut. sg. used adverbially, 'hard, strongly' (flýgra hann svá stint)
glossary.stiórnlauso: stiórnlauss — rudderless, without a helm (stiórn 'helm' + -lauss '-less'); here dat. sg. neut.
glossary.stóli: stóll (m.) — seat, chair, high-seat; here dat. sg.
glossary.stóra: stórr — great, big; here acc. pl. masc. (miǫk stóra stafi)
glossary.stóðomk: standa — to stand; here 3rd pl. pret. with the -mk middle ending, 'stood about me'
glossary.stýrir: stýra (+ dat.) — to steer, govern; here 3rd sg. pres., 'governs'
glossary.stǫðvigak: stǫðva — to stop, to stay, to halt; here 1st sg. pres. subjunctive with the enclitic pronoun twice over and the negative between them: stǫðvi + -g- (= -k, the enclitic ek voiced between vowels, as in kennig at 163,2) + -a (negative) + -k (the enclitic ek again). With the free ek before the verb the first person is expressed three times. 'That I do not stop it.'
glossary.suma: sumr — some; here acc. pl. (í suma 'to some')
glossary.sumar: sumr — some; here acc. pl. fem., agreeing with the rúnar of st. 142,1 across the stanza break (ek reist siálfr sumar 'some I carved myself')
glossary.sumbli: sumbl (n.) — an ale-feast, a banquet; by extension the drink served at it; here dat. sg. (sumbli frá 'away from the ale-feast')
glossary.sumr: sumr — some one, one (of several); nom. sg. masc. (sumr … sumr 'one … another')
glossary.sumt: sumr — some; here neut., 'some (of it)' (sumt var ólagat)
glossary.suttung: Suttungr (m.) — Suttungr, the giant who kept the mead of poetry; here acc. sg.
glossary.sva: svá — so, thus (adv.). Neckel prints sva without the acute at 157,4, though svá at 152,4, 155,4 and 159,6.
glossary.svikinn: svíkia — to betray, cheat, deceive; here past part. acc. sg. masc., 'cheated'
glossary.svinna: svinnr — wise, clever, quick-witted; here weak gen. sg. neut., agreeing with mans (ins svinna mans 'of the clever girl'; man is a neuter noun); the same adjective as sviðr, st. 103,3
glossary.svá: svá — so, thus (adv.; Hón svá gørir 'she works it so', st. 114,1); with a following at, the conjunction 'so that', introducing a result clause with the subjunctive (svá at hon lyki þik liðom, st. 113,7).
glossary.svági: svági — 'so … not, not so' (svá + negative -gi); a defective line follows in Neckel
glossary.svára: svárr — heavy, grievous, weighty; here weak gen. sg. (síns ins svára sefa)
glossary.svæfik: svæfa — to lull to sleep (the causative of sofa 'to sleep'); here 1st sg. pres. with the enclitic -k 'I' (svæfi ek → svæfik)
glossary.svíni: svín (n.) — swine, pig; here dat. sg.
glossary.sylg: sylgr (m.) — a drink, draught; here acc. sg. (sylg um getr 'gets a drink')
glossary.synir: sonr (m.) — son; here nom. pl. (gumna synir 'the sons of men')
glossary.systir: systir (f.) — sister; here nom. sg. (eða min systir sé 'or is my sister')
glossary.sá: sá — that, that one; he (demonstrative pron., nom. sg. masc.); sá er 'he who'; era sá vinr ǫðrom. Also siá — to see; here 1st sg. pret., 'I saw' (sá ek ok þagðak, st. 111; ek sá einom hal, st. 118) — two different words with the same form.
glossary.sæ: sær (m.) — the sea; here acc. sg. (allan sæ 'all the sea')
glossary.sæll: sæll — fortunate, happy, blessed (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.sællifðom: sællifðr — living well, blessed; here dat. pl. as substantive, 'the well-living'; reading disputed
glossary.særir: særa — to wound, to hurt; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.sæva: sær (m.) — sea; here gen. pl. (lítilla sæva 'of small seas')
glossary.sævar: sær (m.) — sea; here gen. sg. (til sævar kømr 'comes to the sea')
glossary.sé: vera — to be; pres. subjunctive, 3rd sg. AND 3rd pl. alike (sg. sé, sér, sé; pl. sém, séð, sé). 3rd sg. at þótt sé, at en sé ofblótit and en sé ofsóit (st. 145,2 and 145,5), and at eða min systir sé (st. 163,9); 3rd PL. at þó sé þér góð (st. 162,7), where the subject is the neuter plural lióð of 162,4 and góð, nýt, þǫrf are nom. pl. neut. ALSO siá — to see; 1st sg. pres., 'I see', which is what it is in the conditional opening of four charms: ef ek sé af fári skotinn (150,2), ef ek sé hávan loga (152,2), ef ek sé túnriðor (155,2), ef ek sé á tré uppi (157,2). Two different words with the same form, and in the Ljóðatal the verb of seeing is the commoner one.
glossary.séi: vera — to be; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'be' (æva til snotr séi 'let him never be too wise')
glossary.séir: vera — to be; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'you be' (nema á niósn séir). Neckel prints the i in italic as an editorial expansion; the Codex Regius reads sér.
glossary.sék: siá — to see; here 1st sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun -k 'I' (sé ek → sék), preceded by the expletive particle of
glossary.sér: (1) siá — to see; here 3rd sg. pres., 'sees, looks' (ey sér til gildis giǫf 'ever a gift looks to a return', st. 145,3). (2) sik — oneself; dat. reflexive, 'for himself, to himself'. (3) vera — to be, 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'you be' (nema þú siálfom þér sér, st. 126,7). Three distinct words share this form; the Rúnatal adds the first.
glossary.sét: vera — to be; sét = sé + -t, 'be not' (subjunctive + neg.); þótt hann sét væddr til vel
glossary.sétta: sétti — sixth; here weak acc. sg. neut. (it sétta). The Ljóðatal counts its charms with the formula Þat kann ek it <ordinal>, set at st. 147 and running unbroken to st. 163.
glossary.sétti: sétti — sixth (ordinal); inn sétti (dagr) 'the sixth day'
glossary.sín: sinn — his own; here nom./acc. pl. neut. (ørlǫg sín 'his fate')
glossary.sínom: sinn — his own; here dat. (vápnom sínom 'from his weapons'; vin sínom 'to his friend')
glossary.síns: sinn — his or her own (reflexive possessive); gen. sg. At st. 105 it refers to Gunnlǫð, not to the speaker: síns ins heila hugar 'for her whole heart'.
glossary.síð: síð — late (adv.); of alinn síð 'born late'; til síð 'too late'
glossary.síðr: síðr — less (comparative adv.); in a clause of this shape 'the less', i.e. so that … not, lest
glossary.sóa: sóa (+ dat.) — to sacrifice, to slay, to make away with (infinitive); with the dative of the victim, as of Bǫlverkr at st. 109 (hefði hánom Suttungr of sóit).
glossary.sóit: sóa — to sacrifice, to destroy, to make away with; here past part.
glossary.sólar: sól (f.) — sun; here gen. sg. (sólar sýn 'the sight of the sun')
glossary.sólginn: sólginn — ravenous, famished; here nom. sg. masc. (sem sólginn sé 'as if famished')
glossary.sólhvíta: sólhvítr — sun-white, radiantly pale (sól 'sun' + hvítr 'white'); here acc. sg. fem.
glossary.sótta: sœkia — to seek, visit, go to; here 1st sg. pret., 'I sought out'
glossary.sóttom: sótt (f.) — sickness, disease; here dat. pl.
glossary.søfr: sofa — to sleep; here 3rd sg. pres. (um morgin søfr 'sleeps through the morning')
glossary.sønir: sonr (m.) — son; here nom. pl. (ýta sønir 'sons of men'); Neckel's spelling of synir
glossary.sú: sá — that; here nom. sg. fem., 'that one, which' (sú er stendr)
glossary.sút: sút (f.) — sorrow, grief; here acc. sg. (sút ala 'nurse sorrow')
glossary.sútom: sút (f.) — care, sickness, grief; here dat. pl.
glossary.sýn: sýn (f.) — sight, seeing; here nom./acc. sg. (sólar sýn 'the sight of the sun')
glossary.sýnst: sýnn — visible, evident; here superlative neut., 'most evident' (á siálfom sýnst)
glossary.sýtir: sýta — to grieve, mourn; here 3rd sg. pres. (sýtir við giǫfom 'grieves at gifts')
glossary.sǫk: sǫk (f.) — a cause at law, a charge, a ground of accusation; here acc. sg.
glossary.sǫkom: sǫk (f.) — a charge, a lawsuit, a cause of strife; here dat. pl. (við sǫkom ok sorgom 'against strifes and sorrows')
glossary.taka: taka — to take, to receive (infinitive); hlátr taka 'receive laughter'; taka við e-u 'to receive something, to take charge of it', the verb understood throughout the remedy-catalogue of st. 137 (fold skal við flóði taka). The remedial force — 'absorbs, counteracts' — is inferred from the catalogue, not given by the lexicon; and English 'take against' is a false friend.
glossary.tamr: tamr — tame, broken in (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.taugreptan: taugreptr — raftered with cords/withies (of a humble roof); here acc. sg. masc. (taugreptan sal)
glossary.teitom: teitr — merry, frisky, high-spirited; here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.tekr: taka — to take; here 3rd sg. pres. (flótta tekr 'takes to flight'; iǫrð tekr við ǫlðri 'earth takes up drink').
glossary.telia: telia — to count, to reckon up, to recite in order (infinitive); telia fyrir e-m 'to count over for someone'
glossary.teygða: teygia — to draw on, entice, lure; here 1st sg. pret.
glossary.teygðo: teygia — to draw on, entice, lure; here the imperative with the enclitic pronoun (teyg þú → teygðo). Twice in these counsels, with the dative of interest þér 'to yourself' and an at-phrase naming what the person is drawn into — postposed at 115 (annars kono … eyrarúno at), preposed at 120 (góðan mann … at gamanrúnom). The same verb of Óðinn's own attempt at st. 102.
glossary.til: til — to, toward; (with gen.) of; til kynnis 'to a visit'; til geðs 'of his mind'
glossary.tryggr: tryggr — trusting; also trusty, faithful (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.tryggva: tryggr — trusty, faithful; here weak gen. sg. (ins tryggva vinar 'the trusty friend's')
glossary.tryggðom: tryggð (f.) — good faith, a pledge, a truce; here dat. pl.
glossary.tré: tré (n.) — a tree; a piece of timber, and so the beam or bar of a door; nom. sg. (st. 136,1) and dat. sg. after á (á tré uppi 'up in a tree', st. 157,2) — the noun does not change its form.
glossary.trémǫnnom: trémaðr (m.) — a wooden man, figure; here dat. pl. (tveim trémǫnnom 'two wooden men')
glossary.trøðr: troða — to tread, walk on; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.trúa: trúa (+ dat.) — to trust, believe in (infinitive)
glossary.trúi: trúa (+ dat.) — to trust; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let (him) trust'
glossary.trúir: trúa (+ dat.) — to trust, believe; here 2nd/3rd sg. pres. (vel trúir 'trust well'; illa trúir 'trust ill')
glossary.tvau: tveir — two; here neut. (tvau lær 'two hams')
glossary.tveim: tveir — two; here dat. (tveim trémǫnnom 'two wooden men')
glossary.tveir: tveir — two (nom. masc.); Tveir ro eins heriar
glossary.tvær: tveir — two; here acc. fem. (tvær geitr 'two goats')
glossary.tvévetrom: tvévetr — two winters old (tvé- 'two' + vetr 'winter'); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.tælir: tæla — to entice, betray, take in; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.tíunda: tíundi — tenth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.tíva: týr (m.), pl. tívar — a god; here acc. pl., the object of telia (telia tíva fyrir 'to reckon the gods up before'); the acc. and gen. pl. of this word are alike, and the genitives in the stanza are ása ok álfa, governed by allra skil. The plural supplies the ordinary poetic word for the gods.
glossary.tíðir: tíða — to desire (impersonal, with the person in the acc.); here 3rd sg. pres. (ef þik fara tíðir 'if it takes you to travel')
glossary.tólpta: tólpti — twelfth; here weak acc. sg. neut. (Neckel's spelling of tólfti)
glossary.túnriðor: túnriða (f.) — a 'yard-rider' or 'fence-rider', a woman who rides out at night in another shape; here acc. pl.
glossary.uggir: ugga — to fear, dread; here 3rd sg. pres. (uggir hotvetna 'dreads everything')
glossary.um: um — about, concerning (prep. + dat. or acc.; um ráðom þǫgðo 'were silent about counsels'; um sanna sǫk 'over a true charge'). With the dative also spatially 'over, above': sal um sessmǫgom (st. 152,3) 'the hall over the bench-companions'. Also an old expletive particle before verbs (um getr, um geta, um farit), which continues here too: um stendr (154,2), er einn um kann (163,5).
glossary.una: una (+ dat.) — to be content with, to take pleasure in (infinitive)
glossary.und: und — under (prep.). With the DATIVE, of rest or disposal: und hvǫtom 'at the disposal of the vigorous'. With the ACCUSATIVE, of motion: und randir ek gel (st. 156,4), the chant carried in under the raised shield-rims.
glossary.undaðr: unda — to wound; here past part. nom. sg. masc., agreeing with the subject ek (geiri undaðr 'wounded with a spear')
glossary.ungan: ungr — young; here acc. sg. masc., agreeing with þegn
glossary.unnit: vinna — to work, perform, accomplish; here past part.; eið vinna 'to swear an oath'
glossary.uppi: uppi — up, out, exposed (adv.); uppi er geð 'the mind is laid bare'
glossary.upploki: upplok (n.) — an opening, an unlocking; here dat. sg. (ǫllom at upploki 'for opening to everyone')
glossary.urðar: Urðr (f.) — Urðr, the norn of what has become; here gen. sg. (Urðar brunni 'Urðr's well', the spring of fate beneath the world-tree)
glossary.urðot: verða — to become; urðot = urðu + suffixed negative -at, 'did not become' (3rd pl. past)
glossary.vakin: vekia — to wake, to rouse (causative); here past part. fem. sg., 'roused, wakened'
glossary.vakir: vaka — to be awake, keep watch; here 3rd sg. pres., 'lies awake'
glossary.val: valr (m.) — the slain (collective, of a battlefield); here dat. sg. (val nýfeldom 'the newly slain')
glossary.valtastr: valtr — unstable, fickle; here superlative, 'most fickle' (valtastr vina 'most fickle of friends')
glossary.vamma: vamm (n.) — blemish, fault; here gen. pl. (vamma vanr 'free of faults')
glossary.vanr: vanr (+ gen.) — lacking, wanting, without; nom. sg. masc. (vamma vanr 'lacking in faults'; lióða þessa … lengi vanr vera, st. 162,4–6, 'long be wanting these songs'). Not to be confused with the other vanr, 'accustomed to', which takes the dative — at 162 the genitive lióða þessa settles it, and the line withholds the charms rather than promising them.
glossary.vant: vanr — lacking, wanting; here neut. sg. (fás er fróðom vant 'little is wanting to the wise')
glossary.var: vera — to be; here 3rd sg. past, 'was' (sem var 'as it was')
glossary.varan: varr — wary, on one's guard; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.varastr: varr — wary; here superlative nom. sg. masc., 'warest'
glossary.varaz: varask (+ acc.) — to beware, guard against; here 3rd sg. pres. middle (við víg varaz 'guards against war')
glossary.vari: varr — wary, cautious; here weak masc., 'the wary' (inn vari gestr)
glossary.varir: vara — to expect, foresee; here 3rd sg. pres. (en varir 'than one expects')
glossary.vark: vera — to be; here old 1st sg. past, 'I was' (ek fiǫtraðr vark)
glossary.varð: verða — to become; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'became' (ǫlr ek varð 'drunk I became')
glossary.vatni: vatn (n.) — water; here dat. sg., governed by verpa
glossary.vatz: vatn (n.) — water; here gen. sg. (vatz er þǫrf 'there is need of water')
glossary.vaxanda: vaxa — to grow, rise, wax; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'rising'
glossary.vaða: vaða — to wade; of a missile, to drive on through the air (infinitive)
glossary.vega: vegr (m.) — way, road; here gen. pl. (villr vega 'lost of the ways')
glossary.vegir: vegr (m.) — way, road; here nom. pl.
glossary.vegnest: vegnest (n.) — journey-provisions, road-food (vegr 'way' + nest 'provisions'); here nom./acc. sg.
glossary.vegom: vegr (m.) — way, road; here dat. pl. (á vegom úti 'out on the roads')
glossary.vegr: vegr (m.) — way, road; here nom. sg. (vegr, er vetki trøðr 'the road that nothing treads', st. 119,8). The Codex Regius reads the genitive vegs, which will not construe with vex; Neckel prints the nominative. ALSO, and this is the word at st. 125,8, vega 'to fight, to strike, to deal a blow', 3rd sg. pres. (þá er inn verri vegr 'when the worse man strikes'; daufr vegr ok dugir, st. 71) — two different words with the same form, and at 125,8 only the verb makes the couplet cohere.
glossary.vegra: vega — to carry, bear (a load); vegra = vegr + suffixed negative -a, '(he) carries not'
glossary.veit: vita — to know; here 3rd sg. pres., 'knows'
glossary.veita: vita — to know; veita = veit + suffixed negative -a, '(he) knows not'
glossary.veitstu: vita — to know; veitstu = veizt + þú, 'do you know, know thou'
glossary.vel: vel — well (adv.); at verða vel 'to turn out well'; vel trúir 'trust well'
glossary.vellanda: vella — to boil, well up; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'boiling'
glossary.velli: vǫllr (m.) — field, open ground; here dat. sg. (velli at 'on the field')
glossary.ver: vera — to be; here 2nd sg. imperative, 'be' (ver þú aldregi 'never be'; ver þú við ǫl varastr 'be warest with ale').
glossary.verir: vera — to be; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'may you be' (skósmiðr þú verir, st. 126,5). The prohibition is carried by the né of the following line, which negates both members: 'be not a shoemaker nor a shaft-maker' — there is no negative word in line 5 itself. A related but not identical shape at st. 135,5–6, where né coordinates an infinitive under ne with a finite verb; here it coordinates a finite verb with a bare noun. verir belongs to the ver- subjunctive inherited from the older vesa; the suppletive sé- subjunctive of the same verb turns up two lines later at 126,7 (sér).
glossary.verk: verk (n.) — work, deed; here nom. sg. (verk … verks leitaði)
glossary.verka: verk (n.) — work, deed; here gen. sg. (síns verka 'of his work')
glossary.verki: verk (n.) — work, deed; here dat. sg. of source (af verki 'from a deed')
glossary.verkom: verk (n.) — work, deed; here dat. pl. (af verkom vel 'in good deeds')
glossary.verks: verk (n.) — work, deed; here gen. sg., the object of leita (verks leitaði 'sought out a deed')
glossary.vero: vera — to be; here a verbal noun/subjunctive, 'a nook to stay in' (í vá vero); reading uncertain
glossary.verpa: verpa (+ dat.) — to throw, to cast; verpa vatni á 'to cast water over', the water-pouring the sagas describe at the naming of a child (ausa vatni), generally taken to be older than Christian baptism; at st. 158,2–3 it is done to a þegn ungan, a young man rather than an infant (infinitive)
glossary.verr: verr — worse (comparative adv.); mart gengr verr. ALSO veria — to wrap, to enclose, to fold about; 3rd sg. pres., which is the word at st. 163,8, er mik armi verr 'who wraps me in her arm', where the dative armi is the instrument and only a verb can govern it. Two different words with the same form.
glossary.verra: verri — worse; here neut. comparative (vegnest verra 'a worse provision') and acc. sg. masc. (við þér verra mann 'with a man worse than you').
glossary.verri: verri — worse (comparative of illr); here nom. sg. fem. and nom. sg. masc. with the article (inn verri 'the worse man').
glossary.versnar: versna — to worsen, grow worse; here 3rd sg. pres. (versnar vinskapr 'the friendship sours')
glossary.verða: verða — to become; to turn out (infinitive); at verða vel 'to turn out well'; also 3rd pl. pres. (gialti glíkir verða gumna synir).
glossary.verðar: verðr (m.) — meal; here gen. sg. (til verðar kømr 'comes to a meal')
glossary.verði: verðr (m.) — meal; here dat. sg. (um verði glissir 'sneers over the meal')
glossary.verðit: verða — to become; here with the suffixed negative -t, 'let (a man) not become'; the Codex Regius was written verðr and corrected to verðit
glossary.verðr: verða — to become; 3rd sg. pres. (at augabragði verðr). Also impersonal with a dative of the person, 'there comes to be, befalls': ef mér verðr þǫrf mikil 'if great need comes upon me' (st. 148,2), víti verðr. The impersonal construction was not spelled out.
glossary.verðu: verða — to become; here 2nd sg. imperative with the enclitic -ðu 'you'. Neckel prints verðu with the Codex Regius; Finnur Jónsson reads verð.
glossary.vetki: vættki (vetki) — nothing, not a whit; also, as the subject of a verb, 'nothing, nobody' (vegr, er vetki trøðr 'the road that nothing treads'). Elsewhere er vetki veit 'who knows nothing'; þess vetki vífs 'nothing at all of that woman'. Neckel prints the final i of the st. 102 occurrence in italic as an editor's correction; the Codex Regius reads vetkis.
glossary.vex: vaxa — to grow; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.veðri: veðr (n.) — weather; here dat. sg. (veðri á sió róa 'row out to sea in fair weather')
glossary.vil: vilia — to will, to want; here 1st sg. pres., 'I want'
glossary.vildu: vilia — to will, want; vildu = vill + þú, 'you would/want' (vildu … geta)
glossary.vilia: (1) vilia — to will, to want; here 3rd pl. pres. (þeir er vilia læknar lifa 'those who want to live as healers', st. 147,3). (2) vili (m.) — will, desire, pleasure; dat. sg. (vísom vilia frá 'away from a sure pleasure', st. 99). The inherited entry had only the noun.
glossary.vill: vilia — to will, want; here 2nd/3rd sg. pres. (sá er annars vill 'who wants another's')
glossary.villar: villr — astray, lost, bewildered; here nom. pl. fem., agreeing with þær, and taking the genitive of what one strays from. R reads villir; villar is Lüning's, and Neckel prints the editorial a in italic.
glossary.villat: vilia — to will, want; here 2nd sg. pres. with the suffixed negative -at. Neckel prints vill-at with the older 2nd sg. vill, where the usual form is vilt (ef þú vilt, st. 98).
glossary.villr: villr — astray, lost; here nom. sg. masc. (villr vega 'lost of the ways')
glossary.vilmæli: vilmæli (n.) — fair words, flattering speech (vil- 'will, desire' + mál 'speech'); here dat. sg.
glossary.vilmǫgom: vilmǫgr (m.) — a genuine crux, found here and almost nowhere else, with two possible parents. Cleasby–Vigfússon give víl-mǫgr, pl. vílmegir, 'a son of toil, a bondsman' (víl 'toil, misery'), which would put the sage of st. 134 among the servants. Against that stands a compound of vil 'entrails' (cf. vil-magi 'the maw'), giving gut-bags hung up to dry, which suits the company of hides and dried skins; the layers follow the second on the strength of the context. Here dat. pl. Nobody is sure.
glossary.vilstígr: vilstígr (m.) — 'the path of desire' (vil- 'will, desire' + stígr 'path'); nom. sg. Neckel's reading; Grundtvig and the newer editors print vílstígr 'path of woe', and the collision may be intended.
glossary.vilt: vilia — to will, want; 2nd sg. pres., 'you want' (ef þú vilt þér mæla man, st. 98; cf. 3rd sg. vill, ef hann vill margfróðr vera, st. 103). At st. 124,6 (er vilt eitt segir) the word is not the verb: it is taken either as the neuter of villr 'false' — reading Neckel's vilt as a single-l spelling of villt — or as connected with vili 'what pleases' ('says only what is agreeable'), taking the word as it stands. A crux; both readings are current.
glossary.vin: vinr (m.) — friend; the dative and accusative singular are both vin; here acc. sg. at 119,5 (ef þú vin átt 'if you have a friend') and dat. sg. at 121,5 (vin þínom 'to your friend'); also óbrigðra vin 'a more faithful friend'.
glossary.vina: vinr (m.) — friend; here gen. pl. (valtastr vina 'most fickle of friends')
glossary.vinar: vinr (m.) — friend; here gen. sg. (til illz vinar 'to a bad friend'; vinar vinr 'a friend's friend')
glossary.vindga: vindugr — windy, wind-blown; here weak dat. sg. masc. (vindga meiði á 'on a windy tree'). The Corpus poeticum boreale and Finnur Jónsson read the two words as one compound instead: Vingameiði (C, capitalised, hence a name) or vingameiði (J, lowercase, hence an appellative).
glossary.vini: vinr (m.) — friend; here acc. pl. (viðhlæiendr vini 'laughing friends')
glossary.vinir: vinr (m.) — friend; here nom. pl. (vinir gleðiaz 'friends gladden each other')
glossary.vinnaz: vinna — to work; to last, suffice; here infinitive middle (er vinnaz megi 'which may last')
glossary.vinnk: vinna — to work, to do, to bring about; here 1st sg. pres. with the enclitic -k 'I' (vinn ek → vinnk)
glossary.vinom: vinr (m.) — friend; here dat. pl. (illom vinom 'bad friends')
glossary.virgilná: virgilnár (m.) — a corpse on the halter, a hanged man (virgill 'rope, noose' + nár 'corpse'); here acc. sg.
glossary.virði: virði (n.) — food, provisions, a meal; here dat. sg. (at virði vrekaz 'clash at the meal', st. 32; fástu at virði vel 'get yourself well provided with food', st. 116).
glossary.vitandi: vita — to know; here pres. participle, 'knowing' (vitandi vits 'having understanding of wit')
glossary.vitaðr: vita — to mark out, assign, point the way; here past part. masc. sg.
glossary.viti: vita — to know; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'has/minds' (geðs viti 'minds his sense')
glossary.vitka: vitka — to blame, find fault; here infinitive (skylit þann vitka 'should not blame him'); reading uncertain
glossary.vito: vita — to know; here 3rd pl. pres., 'know' (Hiarðir þat vito 'herds know that')
glossary.vits: vit (n.) — wit, sense; here gen. sg. (vitandi vits 'knowing of wit')
glossary.vitz: vit (n.) — wit; here gen. sg. (vitz er þǫrf 'there is need of wit'); Neckel spells vitz
glossary.við: viðr (m.) — wood, tree, timber; acc. sg. (við hǫggva 'hew wood'). Also the preposition við, with three constructions. (a) + DAT. of price or exchange after selia, 'for, in exchange for': Við hleifi mik seldo … né við hornigi (st. 139,1–2) — the construction that makes the line resist construal, since nothing here is bought or sold; some take it as a looser instrumental 'with'. (b) + ACC. 'against, towards, in the face of': við eld 'by the fire'; við man spialla 'talk with a girl'; ver þú við ǫl varastr (131,7); hapts við mína heiptmǫgo 'of a fetter against my foes' (148,3). (c) + DAT. in the remedy-catalogue of st. 137, with two distinct uses. After taka it belongs to the fixed phrasal verb taka við e-u 'to receive, to take in', where the dative names the thing RECEIVED and not the thing opposed: iǫrð tekr við ǫlðri (137,7) 'earth takes up drink', fold skal við flóði taka (137,15) 'land shall take up the flood'. Elsewhere in the same catalogue, with the verb elided, bare við + dat. is the remedial 'against': eldr við sóttom, eik við abbindi, ax við fiǫlkyngi, en við bǫlvi rúnar (137,8–14); so too hiálpa … við sǫkom ok sorgom (146,9). The contrast that holds is acc. 'against, towards' vs dat. after taka 'receive'; English 'take against' fits neither and is a false friend.
glossary.viðar: viðr (m.) — wood, tree, timber; gen. sg. (þess viðar 'of that timber'). At st. 151,3, á rótom rás viðar, it stands as the second half of a compound Neckel prints open, rásviðr, which no editor has securely construed — see the note to that stanza.
glossary.viðhlæiendr: viðhlæiandi (m.) — one who laughs with another, a flatterer; here acc./nom. pl. (pres. part.)
glossary.viði: viðr (m.) — tree, wood, timber; here dat. sg.
glossary.viðrgefendr: viðrgefandi (m.) — one who gives in return; here nom. pl. (pres. part.)
glossary.viðrir: viðra — to be weather, change (of weather); here 3rd sg. pres. (fiǫlð um viðrir 'the weather shifts much')
glossary.vrekaz: reka — to drive; here 3rd pl. pres. middle, 'clash, come to blows' (at virði vrekaz)
glossary.vá: vá (f.) — a nook, corner, recess; here acc./dat. sg. (í vá vero 'a nook to stay in'); reading uncertain
glossary.váfa: váfa — to swing, to dangle, to hover (infinitive, in an accusative-and-infinitive after sé)
glossary.váfir: váfa — to swing, to hover, to sway; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.vági: vágr (m.) — wave, sea, creek; here dat. sg.
glossary.válaðs: válaðr (m.) — a destitute, wretched man; here gen. sg. (válaðs vera 'the refuge of the destitute')
glossary.váloðom: váluðr (m.) — a wretch, a beggar, a man with nothing; here dat. pl.
glossary.vánar: ván (f.) — hope, expectation; here gen. sg. (vánar vǫl 'the staff of expectation', the beggar's staff)
glossary.vápn: vápn (n.) — weapon; here nom. pl. (bítat þeim vápn 'weapons bite them not')
glossary.vápnom: vápn (n.) — weapon; here dat. pl. (vápnom sínom 'from his weapons')
glossary.vár: vá — to blame, find fault, reproach; here 3rd sg. pres. (vár þik engi maðr 'no man will reproach you')
glossary.váða: váð (f.) — cloth, clothing; here gen. sg. (matar ok váða 'of food and clothing')
glossary.váðir: váð (f.) — cloth, garment; here nom./acc. pl. (Váðir mínar 'my clothes')
glossary.váðom: váð (f.) — cloth, garment; here dat. pl. (vápnom ok váðom 'with weapons and clothes')
glossary.væddr: væða — to clothe; here past participle masc., 'clothed, clad' (væddr til vel 'too well clad')
glossary.væni: væni (n.) — likelihood, expectation; here nom. sg. (handar væni 'the likelihood of a hand')
glossary.væra: vera — to be; here 1st sg. pret. subjunctive, 'I would have been, would have come'
glossary.væri: vera — to be; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'were, would be' (at ei væri 'that … was not')
glossary.vættak: vætta — to expect, await; here 1st sg. pret. with the enclitic -k 'I' (vætta ek → vættak)
glossary.vélir: vél (f.) — a wile, a trick; also, concretely, a contrivance or engine, which is what makes bíta apt of it; here nom. pl., paired with vápn as a second thing that fails to bite.
glossary.vés: vé (n.) — a sanctuary, a holy place; here gen. sg.
glossary.vífs: víf (n.) — woman, wife; here gen. sg. (þess vetki vífs 'nothing at all of that woman')
glossary.víg: víg (n.) — battle, war, killing; here acc. sg. (við víg varaz 'guards against war')
glossary.vígdiarft: vígdiarfr — bold in war; here neut., 'war-bold'
glossary.vígdrótt: vígdrótt (f.) — war-band, the fighting household (víg 'battle' + drótt 'retinue'); nom. sg.
glossary.víl: víl (n.) — misery, woe (nom./acc. sg.); allt er víl 'all is woe'
glossary.vísom: víss — certain, sure; here dat. sg. masc. (vísom vilia frá)
glossary.víti: víti (n.) — harm, penalty, mishap; here nom./acc. sg. (víti verðr 'harm befalls')
glossary.vóro: vera — to be; here 3rd pl. pret., 'were'
glossary.vǫl: vǫlr (m.) — a staff, rod; here acc. sg. (vánar vǫl 'the beggar's staff')
glossary.vǫlo: vǫlva (f.) — seeress, prophetess; here gen. sg. (vǫlo vilmæli 'a seeress's fair words')
glossary.vǫrom: varr — wary; here dat. pl. (víti vǫrom 'harm to the wary')
glossary.yfir: yfir — over, above (prep.); yfir ǫlðrom þrumir 'broods over ale-feasts'
glossary.ynði: ynði (n.) — delight, contentment, joy; here nom. sg.
glossary.yrkendr: yrkiandi (m.) — a worker, labourer; here acc. pl. (á yrkendr fá 'has few workers')
glossary.á: á — on, upon, at (prep. + dat. or acc.); frequently postposed after its noun in this part (þular stóli á 'on the sage's seat', st. 111,2; lopti á, st. 155,3; á floti, st. 154,3). With the ACCUSATIVE after verbs of directing attention: hlýdda ek á manna mál (st. 111,6), cf. teygða ek á flærðir (st. 102). With the ACCUSATIVE also of the surface something is thrown or poured onto: verpa vatni á, with þegn ungan of the line before as the object of the postposed á (st. 158,2–3), 'to cast water over a young man'. In adverbial phrases of state (á niósn 'on the watch', st. 112,6; á fialli 'on the fell', st. 116,5). Also 'has, owns' (3rd sg. of eiga: siálfr um á).
glossary.álfa: álfr (m.) — an elf; here gen. pl.
glossary.álfom: álfr (m.) — an elf; here dat. pl., one of the ranked classes of beings in both places (en fyr álfom Dáinn 'and Dáinn for the elves', st. 143,3; en álfom frama, st. 160,4)
glossary.án: án — without (prep.); án við lǫst 'without vice'
glossary.ár: ár — early (adv.); ár skal rísa 'should rise early'
glossary.ársánom: ársáinn — sown early in the year (ár 'early' + sáinn, past part. of sá 'to sow'); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.ása: áss (m.) — one of the Æsir, a god; here gen. pl.
glossary.ásom: áss (m.) — one of the Æsir, a god; here dat. pl. (Óðinn með ásom 'Óðinn among the Æsir', st. 143,1; afl gól hann ásom 'he chanted strength to the Æsir', st. 160,3)
glossary.ást: ást (f.) — love, affection; here acc. sg.
glossary.ástar: ást (f.) — love; here gen. sg. governed by firna
glossary.ásviðr: Ásviðr (m.) — Ásviðr, here the rune-carver of the giants; nom. sg. The name appears nowhere else in the Codex Regius poems, and the paper manuscripts read Alsviðr.
glossary.átt: eiga — to own, have; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you have' (ef þú vin átt)
glossary.átta: átti — eighth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.áttiánda: áttiándi — eighteenth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.æva: æva — never (adv.); æva þegir 'is never silent'
glossary.ævagi: ævagi — never ever (æva + emphatic -gi); kann ævagi 'never knows'
glossary.ís: íss (m.) — ice; here acc. sg., one of the objects of leyfa (nom. is íss)
glossary.óauðigr: óauðigr — not rich, poor (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.óbeðit: biðia — to ask, to pray; here past part. neut. with the negative prefix ó-, used impersonally (betra er óbeðit 'better it is unprayed'). The verb is the biðia of st. 144,5, and we keep 'pray' in both places.
glossary.óbrigðra: óbrigðr — unfailing, faithful; here comparative, 'a more faithful' (óbrigðra vin)
glossary.óbryddom: óbryddr — unspiked, not calked (ó- 'un-' + bryddr, of shoeing a horse with ice-spikes); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.ódælla: ódæll — difficult, hard to deal with; here comparative neut., 'harder' (ódælla er við þat)
glossary.ógott: ógott — no good, ill; here neut. as noun (sér ógott um gelr 'sings itself no good')
glossary.ógǫrla: ógǫrla — not clearly, not exactly (ó- 'un-' + gǫrla 'fully, closely'; cf. gǫrva, st. 102)
glossary.óhǫpp: óhapp (n.) — mishap, misfortune, ill luck; here acc. pl. (óhǫpp at þér 'mishaps concerning you')
glossary.ókunnom: ókunnr — unknown, unfamiliar; here dat. sg. (í ókunnom stað 'in an unknown place')
glossary.ókynnis: ókynni (n.) — discourtesy, bad manners; here gen. sg. (ókynnis vár 'blame for discourtesy')
glossary.ólagat: ólagaðr — not brewed, unprepared; here neut. (sumt var ólagat 'some was not brewed')
glossary.óminnis: óminni (n.) — forgetfulness, oblivion; here gen. sg. (Óminnis hegri 'heron of forgetfulness')
glossary.ónýtr: ónýtr — useless, of no use (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.ór: ór — out of, from (prep.); annars brióstom ór 'out of another's breast'
glossary.órir: óra — to quarrel, be at odds; here 3rd sg. pres. (gestr við gest órir 'guest quarrels with guest'); reading uncertain
glossary.ósent: senda — to send; here past part. neut. with the negative prefix ó-, used impersonally (betra er ósent 'better it is unsent')
glossary.óskǫp: óskǫp (n. pl.) — an ill fate, a monstrous thing, ruin (ó- 'un-' + skǫp 'what is shaped or fated')
glossary.ósnotrs: ósnotr — unwise, foolish; here gen. sg. masc. (ósnotrs aðal 'the nature of the unwise')
glossary.ósvinna: ósvinnr — unwise, foolish (the negative of sviðr/svinnr); here weak acc. sg. masc. Formally ambiguous: ósvinna is also the strong acc. pl. masc., and apa is both acc. sg. and acc. pl. of api, so við ósvinna apa could be 'with unwise apes'. The singular is read here on the pattern of the parallel counsel at st. 125,6 (við þér verra mann).
glossary.óvinar: óvinr (m.) — enemy; here gen. sg. (óvinar síns 'of his enemy')
glossary.óvinir: óvinr (m.) — enemy, foe (ó- 'un-' + vinr 'friend'); here nom. pl.
glossary.óvíst: óvíss — uncertain; here neut., 'uncertain' (óvíst er at vita 'it is uncertain to know')
glossary.óðni: Óðinn (m.) — Óðinn; here dat. sg. (gefinn Óðni 'given to Óðinn')
glossary.óðom: óðr — raging, furious, frantic; here dat. sg. masc. (í byr óðom 'in a raging wind')
glossary.óðrerir: Óðrerir (m.) — Óðrerir, the mead of poetry, or the vessel that holds it — the sources differ; the name means something like 'stirrer of the spirit' (nom. sg.)
glossary.óðrøri: Óðrerir (m.) — Óðrerir, the mead of poetry or the vessel that holds it — the sources differ; the name means something like 'stirrer of the spirit'. Here dat. sg. Neckel prints the slashed ø; the Codex Regius reads Óðreri, Munch Óðrœri. Cf. st. 107.
glossary.óþǫrf: óþarfr — needless, useless, of no help (ó- 'un-' + þarfr 'needful'); here nom. pl. neut., agreeing with mál
glossary.øng: engi — none, no; here nom. sg. fem. (øng er sótt verri 'no sickness is worse'); Neckel spells the stem with ø
glossary.øngo: engi — none, nothing; here dat. sg. neut. (sér øngo at una 'to be content with nothing')
glossary.ørlǫg: ørlǫg (n. pl.) — fate, destiny; here acc. (ørlǫg sín 'his fate')
glossary.úti: úti — out, outside (adv.); á vegom úti 'out on the roads'
glossary.ýta: ýtar (m. pl.) — men; here gen. pl. (ýta sønir 'sons of men')
glossary.þagalt: þagall — silent, reserved, discreet; here neut., 'discreet' (Þagalt ok hugalt)
glossary.þagðak: þegia — to be silent; here 1st sg. pret. with the enclitic -k 'I' (þagða ek → þagðak)
glossary.þakinna: þakinn — covering, for roofing (past part. of þekia 'to thatch'); here gen. pl. (þakinna næfra 'of roofing-bark')
glossary.þann: sá — that one; him; here acc. sg. masc. (við þann 'to him'; of þann 'about that one')
glossary.þannz: þann es — 'him whom' (þann + relative particle es/er); þannz þú illa trúir
glossary.þarft: þarfr — needful, useful; here neut., 'what is needful' (mæli þarft 'speak what is useful')
glossary.þars: þar es — 'where' (þar + relative particle es/er); þars ek hafða eitt etit
glossary.þat: þat — that, it (neut. demonstrative/pronoun). In the Ljóðatal it is the object of kann in the counting formula, Þat kann ek annat / it þriðia … 'that I know as a second / third …' (st. 147–163), with the ordinal in apposition to it; st. 164 is the poem's close and stands outside the count. At st. 136,5 (eða þat biðia mun) the antecedent is disputed: gender agreement points to tré, the door-beam of line 1, making the door itself the curser; some read it loosely of the man turned away, for whom no neuter noun has been used. Unresolved.
glossary.þats: þat es — 'that which' (þat + relative particle es/er); þats hefir … hugat 'what one has intended'
glossary.þau: þat — that; here nom./acc. pl. neut., agreeing with lióð (Lióð ek þau kann 'Those songs I know')
glossary.þaðan: þaðan — thence, from there (adv.). Neckel's ð is an editorial letter; the Codex Regius reads þatan.
glossary.þegi: þegia — to be silent; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him be silent'
glossary.þegiandi: þegia — to be silent; here pres. part., 'keeping silent'
glossary.þegir: þegia — to be silent; here 3rd sg. pres., 'is silent'
glossary.þegit: þiggia — to receive, accept; here past participle, 'received' (opt þegit 'often received')
glossary.þegn: þegn (m.) — a free man, a retainer, a man; here nom. sg. (ef mik særir þegn, st. 151,2) and acc. sg. (þegn ungan, st. 158,2)
glossary.þeim: sá / þeir — dat., 'to/for him', 'to them', and adjectivally 'that' (á þeim meiði 'on that tree', st. 138,7). At st. 148,6, bítat þeim vápn né vélir, þeim is a dative of possession and disadvantage, NOT the object of bíta (which takes the accusative): the sense is 'their weapons do not bite', the weapons being the foes' own. At st. 134,10 (þeim er hangir með hám) it is dat. sg. masc. picking up belg of the line before, with er as the relative particle. The adjectival use with a noun was missing.
glossary.þeims: þeim es — 'for him who' (þeim + relative particle es/er)
glossary.þeira: sá / þeir — that; they; here gen. pl., 'of those' (orða þeira 'of those words')
glossary.þeirar: sú — that one, she; here gen. sg. fem. (þeirar er 'she who')
glossary.þeiri: sú — that one, she; here dat. sg. fem. (nema þeiri einni 'except to her alone')
glossary.þeirs: þeir es (þeir er) — they who, those who; the relative particle contracted onto the pronoun (Heilir, þeirs hlýddo!)
glossary.þerro: þerra (f.) — a towel, drying-cloth; here gen. sg. (þerro ok þióðlaðar)
glossary.þess: sá — that; here gen. sg., 'of that' (þess fugls 'of that bird'; ókynnis þess 'of this discourtesy')
glossary.þessa: þessi — this; here gen. pl., agreeing with lióða (lióða þessa 'of these songs')
glossary.þesso: þessi — this; here dat. sg. neut. (at þesso trúi ǫllo 'trust in all this')
glossary.þeygi: þeygi — and yet not, nevertheless not
glossary.þiggia: þiggia — to receive, accept (infinitive); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.þiggr: þiggia — to receive, to accept, to take what is offered; here 2nd sg. pres.
glossary.þik: þú — you; here acc. sg., 'you' — including as the accusative of the person in an impersonal construction (ef þik fara tíðir 'if it takes you to travel', st. 116,6) and as the accusative OBJECT of an infinitive governed by another subject (góðr maðr mun þik gørva mega líknfastan, st. 123,5 — the good man does the making, þik is what is made, and líknfastan agrees with þik). Contrast the true accusative-and-infinitives of this part, where the accusative IS the subject: illan mann … óhǫpp at þér vita (st. 117), orð … bíta (st. 118).
glossary.þikkir: þykkia — to seem; here 3rd sg. pres., 'seems' (auði betra þikkir 'seems better than wealth')
glossary.þikkiz: þykkia — to seem; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'thinks himself, seems' (fróðr þikkiz 'seems wise')
glossary.þingi: þing (n.) — assembly, court; here dat. sg. (at þingi kømr 'comes to the assembly')
glossary.þings: þing (n.) — assembly, the public meeting; here gen. sg. governed by gá
glossary.þiófar: þiófr (m.) — a thief; here nom. pl.
glossary.þióð: þióð (f.) — people, nation; the whole community; here nom. sg. (þióð veit 'the people know')
glossary.þióða: þióð (f.) — a people, a nation; here gen. pl. (fyr þióða rǫk)
glossary.þióðans: þióðann (m.) — king, prince, lord; here gen. sg. (þióðans barn 'a prince's child')
glossary.þióðlaðar: þióðlǫð (f.) — a hearty invitation, warm welcome; here gen. sg.
glossary.þióðrørir: Þióðrørir (m.) — Þióðrørir, a dwarf named nowhere else in Norse; here nom. sg. R writes the name as two words, Þióð reyrir; Þióðrørir is Neckel's normalization.
glossary.þola: þola — to endure, suffer (infinitive); þǫrf þola 'suffer want'
glossary.þorpi: þorp (n.) — an open hillock, exposed spot; a hamlet; here dat. sg. (þorpi á 'on a mound')
glossary.þrettánda: þrettándi — thirteenth; here weak acc. sg. neut.
glossary.þrimr: þrír — three; here dat. pl. (þrimr orðom 'with three words')
glossary.þriðia: þriði — third; here weak nom./acc. sg. neut. (þat it þriðia 'that third thing')
glossary.þruma: þruma — to sit still, keep quiet (infinitive); þurrfiallr þruma 'sit quiet and dry'
glossary.þrumir: þruma — to sit torpid, brood, hover; here 3rd sg. pres. (yfir ǫlðrom þrumir 'broods over ale-feasts')
glossary.þræli: þræll (m.) — thrall, bondman; here dat. sg.
glossary.þrír: þrír — three (nom. masc.); ef þrír ero 'if three know'
glossary.þróaz: þróaz — to grow, thrive, swell (middle); here 3rd sg. pres. (metnaðr þróaz 'pride swells')
glossary.þu: þú — you (2nd sg.); Neckel's spelling þu (unaccented)
glossary.þul: þulr (m.) — a sage, a reciter of old lore — the man who speaks þular stóli á at st. 111; here dat. sg.
glossary.þular: þulr (m.) — a sage, a reciter of ancient lore; here gen. sg. (þular stóli á 'on the sage's seat'). The same word as in fimbulþulr, st. 80.
glossary.þundr: Þundr (m.) — Þundr, a name of Óðinn; nom. sg. Capital Þ, not D — there is no Old Norse *Dundr.
glossary.þunno: þunnr — thin; here dat. sg. neut. (þunno hlióði 'with taut/strained hearing')
glossary.þurfo: þurfa — to need, to have need of; here 3rd pl. pres. (er þurfo ýta synir 'which the sons of men need')
glossary.þurra: þurr — dry; here gen. pl. (Þurra skíða 'of dry logs')
glossary.þurrfiallr: þurrfiallr — dry-skinned, i.e. snug and unexposed (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.þveginn: þvá — to wash; here past participle masc., 'washed' (Þveginn ok mettr)
glossary.því: því — for, because (því at); therefore; (instrumental of sá) 'by that'
glossary.þvíat: þvíat — because, for (Neckel writes it as one word)
glossary.þykkiz: þykkia — to seem; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'thinks himself' (Fróðr sá þykkiz)
glossary.þylia: þylia — to recite, chant, mutter over (infinitive)
glossary.þylsk: þylia — to mutter, recite under one's breath; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'mumbles to himself'
glossary.þyrptak: þurfa — to need; þyrptak = þyrfta + -k, 'if I needed' (1st sg. past subjunctive)
glossary.þyrpti: þurfa — to need; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'ought to' (er hann vita þyrpti 'which he ought to know')
glossary.þáfialli: þáfiall (n.) — a fell in the thaw, a thawing mountainside (þá 'thawed ground' + fiall 'fell'); here dat. sg.
glossary.þægi: þiggia — to receive; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'if he accepted' (ef þægi)
glossary.þær: þeir — they; here nom. pl. fem. (nær þær heim skolo 'when they must go home')
glossary.þér: þú — you; dat. sg., 'to you' (ráðomk þér 'I counsel you'; þér er grunr 'you have suspicion'), and the dative of interest, 'for yourself, to yourself' (leitir þér … staðar, st. 112,7; teygðo þér, st. 115,6 and 120,6). After a preposition: óhǫpp at þér 'mishaps concerning you' (st. 117,7). Also the DATIVE OF COMPARISON after a comparative: við þér verra mann (st. 125,6) is 'with a man worse than you', where þér goes with verra and við governs mann.
glossary.þínom: þinn — your, thine; dat. sg. masc. (vin þínom 'to your friend') and dat. pl. (þínom fiándom 'to your foes', st. 127,7). Gering deleted the word at 127,7; Neckel keeps it, and the apparatus gives no reason for the deletion.
glossary.þótti: þykkia — to seem, to be thought; here 3rd sg. pret., 'seemed'
glossary.þóttomz: þykkia — to seem; here 1st sg. past middle, 'I thought myself' (auðigr þóttomz)
glossary.þóttoz: þykkia — to seem; here 3rd pl. past middle, 'they seemed/thought themselves' (rekkar þóttoz)
glossary.þǫgðo: þegia — to be silent; here 3rd pl. pret., 'they were silent'
glossary.þǫll: þǫll (f.) — a young fir, pine (nom. sg.)
glossary.þǫrf: þǫrf (f.) — need; er þǫrf (+ gen.) 'there is need of' (nom. sg.); ef mér verðr þǫrf mikil (st. 148,2). ALSO þarfr — needful, useful (adj.); nom. pl. neut. þǫrf at st. 162,9, standing in a row with góð and nýt and agreeing with the same unspoken plural (þǫrf, ef þú þiggr 'needful, if you receive them'). The compounds allþǫrf and óþǫrf at st. 164,3–4 are this adjective, not the noun.
glossary.œpandi: œpa — to cry out, to shout, to scream; here pres. part., 'crying out'
glossary.œrna: œrinn — abundant, ample; here neut. as adv., 'abundantly, more than enough' (Œrna mælir)
glossary.œrno: œrinn — abundant, ample; here dat. sg. (fé œrno 'ample wealth')
glossary.œðis: œði (n.) — disposition, temper, manner; here gen. sg. (góðs um œðis 'of good manner')
glossary.ǫld: ǫld (f.) — age; the world; men; here nom. sg. (hálf er ǫld 'the world is half')
glossary.ǫll: allr — all; here nom. sg. fem.
glossary.ǫllo: allr — all; here dat. sg. neut.
glossary.ǫllom: allr — all; dat. pl. masc. (ǫllom at upploki 'for opening to everyone'; er ǫllom er nytsamlikt, st. 153,2 'which is useful for all'), and dat. sg. masc. agreeing with a dative object (ǫllom sefa 'all her feeling', st. 161,6).
glossary.ǫlr: ǫlr — drunk, tipsy (nom. sg. masc.); ǫlr ek varð 'drunk I became'
glossary.ǫls: ǫl (n.) — ale; here gen. sg. (ofdrykkia ǫls 'over-drinking of ale')
glossary.ǫlðr: ǫlðr (n.) — ale-feast, drinking-bout; here nom. sg. (ǫlðr batst 'the best of ale-feasts')
glossary.ǫlðri: ǫlðr (n.) — ale-drinking, an ale-feast, drink; here dat. sg. (tekr við ǫlðri 'takes up drink')
glossary.ǫlðrom: ǫlðr (n.) — ale-feast; here dat. pl. (yfir ǫlðrom 'over ale-feasts')
glossary.ǫðrom: annarr — other, another; here dat. sg. (ǫðrom segir 'says to another'; af ǫðrom 'by another')
